simple.meaning: בָּצֵק (bâtsêq) is a Hebrew object word meaning “dough (as swelling by fermentation).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Exodus 12:34. The surrounding context includes family, offering, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּצֵק (H1217) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: בָּצֵק (bâtsêq) / H1217 is traced through Exodus 12:34, Exodus 12:39, 2 Samuel 13:8, Jeremiah 7:18 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading troughs being bound up in their clothes on their shoulders.

majorEvents.label: Offering
majorEvents.evidenceText: The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead the dough, to make cakes to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to other gods, that they may provoke me to anger.

timeline.evidenceText: The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading troughs being bound up in their clothes on their shoulders.

They baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought out of Egypt; for it wasn’t leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, and couldn’t wait, and they had not prepared any food for themselves.
So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house; and he was lying down. She took dough, and kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.

The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead the dough, to make cakes to the queen of the sky, and to pour out drink offerings to other gods, that they may provoke me to anger.
